verses.text: But now the LORD who made you, Jacob, the one who shaped you, Israel, says, “Don't be afraid. I've bought you back. I called you by name. You're mine.
When you go through deep water, I'll be with you. When you cross rivers, they won't sweep over you. When you walk through fire, you won't burn, and the flames won't scorch you.
I'm the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, the one who saves you. I gave Egypt to get you back, and Ethiopia and Seba in your place.
You're precious to me and I honor you. I love you, so I'll give people in your place and nations in exchange for your life.
Don't be afraid. I'm with you. I'll bring your children from the east and gather you from the west.
I'll tell the north, ‘Give them back!’ and the south, ‘Don't hold them back! Bring my sons from far away and my daughters from the ends of the earth.
Bring everyone who carries my name, everyone I created for my glory, everyone I shaped and made.’”
Bring out the people who have eyes but are blind, and people who have ears but are deaf.

Let all the nations gather and all the peoples come together. Which of them can announce this and show us what happened before? Let them bring witnesses who can prove they're right, or let them listen and say, “That's true.”
“You're my witnesses,” says the LORD, “along with the servant I chose, so you can know me, believe me, and understand that I am he. No god was formed before me, and none will come after me.
I myself am the LORD. There's no one besides me who saves.
I announced it, I saved you, and I showed you what would happen. No foreign god was among you. So you're my witnesses,” says the LORD, “and I am God.
I've been the same since the first day. Nobody can snatch anything out of my hand. When I act, who can stop me?”
The LORD, the one who redeems you, the Holy One of Israel, says, “For your sake I've sent to Babylon, and I'll bring them all down as fugitives, even the Chaldeans in the ships they were so proud of.
I am the LORD, your Holy One, the one who made Israel, your King.”
The LORD makes a road through the sea and a path through the mighty waters.
He brings out the chariots and horses, the army and its mighty warriors. They all lie down together and won't get up. They're snuffed out like a wick. He says,
“Quit looking back to what happened before. Don't keep dwelling on the old days.
Look, I'm doing something new! It's already springing up. Can't you see it? I'll even make a road through the wilderness and rivers in the desert.
Wild animals will honor me, the jackals and the ostriches, because I'll give water in the wilderness and rivers in the desert to give my chosen people something to drink.
I made these people for myself so they'd tell the world my praise.
But you haven't called on me, Jacob. You got tired of me, Israel.
You haven't brought me sheep for burnt offerings or honored me with your sacrifices. I haven't weighed you down with offerings or worn you out asking for frankincense.
You haven't spent money on sweet cane for me or given me my fill of the fat from your sacrifices. You've loaded me down with your sins and worn me out with your wrongdoing.
I am the one who wipes your wrongs away for my own sake. I won't remember your sins.
Remind me. Let's argue it out together. Make your case so you can be shown to be right.
Your first father sinned, and your teachers broke faith with me.
So I'll strip the leaders of the sanctuary of their sacred standing. I'll make Jacob a curse and Israel a name people throw around as an insult.”
